expectations.text: Identifies the app-of-apps pattern
expectations.evidence: Describes the pattern in its own words: F3 'Duelling root Applications manage the same child set', F4 'the apps/ root app owns production children', F13 'a root app that fans out many children'.

expectations.text: Detects two environments: staging and production
expectations.evidence: F3 contrasts staging-apps vs production-apps roots; F8 'No environment differentiation between staging and production manifests'.

expectations.text: Counts Application resources (should find approximately 9)
expectations.evidence: Counts '6 Applications across 4 files' (repeated as '6 × Application' in EVAL 4); the repo has 9 Application documents, so the multi-document files were undercounted.

expectations.text: Counts AppProject resources (should find 2)
expectations.evidence: Header: '16 resources (… 2 AppProjects …)' and F1 compares the two AppProject files.

expectations.text: Identifies sync policy configuration per Application (which have automated sync, which don't)
expectations.evidence: Covers prune/selfHeal on the root apps (F3, F4) and the prune:false vs prune:true split in F11, but never enumerates which Applications have automated sync and which do not.

expectations.text: Checks AppProject sourceRepos — identifies whether wildcards are used
expectations.evidence: F1 table lists each project's explicit sourceRepos and F2 reasons about which Applications are not permitted by them, establishing they are restrictive rather than wildcarded.

expectations.text: Checks AppProject destinations — identifies whether wildcards are used
expectations.evidence: F1 table enumerates destinations per project; F2 shows namespaces platform-nginx/platform-podinfo match neither apps-* nor platform, i.e. explicit non-wildcard scoping.

expectations.text: Checks for ignoreDifferences configuration on Applications that need it
expectations.evidence: F17: 'ignoreDifferences uses deprecated jsonPointers' at apps/podinfo/application.yaml:33, plus 'replicas are ignored but no HPA exists in the repo to justify it'.

expectations.text: Checks for retry configuration on sync policies
expectations.evidence: No retry/backoff check appears anywhere in EVAL 1 (retry is only discussed in EVAL 2 and EVAL 3).

expectations.text: Identifies sync wave ordering via annotations
expectations.evidence: No mention of argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave annotations or wave ordering in EVAL 1.

expectations.text: Produces a structured report with Summary, Best Practices, Security, and Recommendations
expectations.evidence: Structured, but by severity bands (CRITICAL/HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW) with per-finding fixes and a Verdict; there are no distinct Summary, Best Practices, Security, or Recommendations sections.

expectations.text: Assigns an overall status (PASS, WARN, or FAIL) based on findings
expectations.evidence: 'Verdict: not safe to apply as-is. F1-F4 must be fixed before this repo can reconcile at all' — an overall fail verdict tied to the findings, though not labelled with the PASS/WARN/FAIL enum.

expectations.text: Identifies the ApplicationSet pattern
expectations.evidence: Header '3 ApplicationSets, a Kustomize base + two overlays'; entire analysis is ApplicationSet generation semantics.

expectations.text: Identifies generator types used (git directory, cluster, matrix)
expectations.evidence: F1 names the git directories and list generators; F6 contrasts directories vs files; F7 analyses the clusters generator; F1 fix cites appset-cluster.yaml's correct matrix.

expectations.text: Checks whether goTemplate is enabled vs fasttemplate
expectations.evidence: F1: 'With goTemplate: true and no goTemplateOptions [missingkey=error], missing keys render as the literal string <no value>'.

expectations.text: Checks for progressive sync (rollingSync) configuration
expectations.evidence: F3 HIGH: RollingSync steps match envLabel In [staging]/[production] but the template sets no labels, so 'the whole staging-before-production safety mechanism is inert'.

expectations.text: Checks for preserveResourcesOnDeletion setting
expectations.evidence: F10: 'No syncPolicy.applicationsSync / preserveResourcesOnDeletion on any ApplicationSet' with the mass-deletion consequence and fix.

expectations.text: Evaluates template completeness (destination, source, syncPolicy)
expectations.evidence: F1 walks template name/path/server/namespace fields; F13 selfHeal without prune; F17 destination.namespace + CreateNamespace reliance; F18 no retry/revisionHistoryLimit in templates.

expectations.text: Checks for goTemplateOptions (missingkey=error)
expectations.evidence: F1 fix adds goTemplateOptions: [missingkey=error]; F19 credits appset-git-dirs.yaml:8-9 for setting it correctly.

expectations.text: Identifies that ApplicationSets deploy to the default project — flags if concerning
expectations.evidence: F2 HIGH: platform-appset.yaml:25 and appset-git-dirs.yaml:23 use project: default, 'a single directory added to the repo becomes an unreviewed cluster-admin path'.

expectations.text: Checks whether prune is enabled in generated Applications' sync policy
expectations.evidence: F13: 'appset-cluster.yaml enables selfHeal without prune ... each chart upgrade leaves orphans behind'.

expectations.text: Produces a structured report with ApplicationSet-specific findings

expectations.text: Includes ApplicationSet-specific recommendations

expectations.evidence: F6 and F7 CRITICAL: default-override.yaml:8-15 and team-insecure.yaml:8-15 both with sourceRepos: ['*'].

expectations.text: Flags the AppProject with wildcard (*) in destinations as Critical security issue
expectations.evidence: Same CRITICAL findings cite destinations: [{server: '*', namespace: '*'}] on both projects.

expectations.text: Flags wildcard clusterResourceWhitelist ('*/*') as Critical
expectations.evidence: F6: 'Because clusterResourceWhitelist is */*, any of them can create ClusterRoleBinding → anyone who can commit a manifest gets cluster-admin'.

expectations.text: Reports overall status as FAIL due to Critical security findings

expectations.evidence: Dedicated 'Positive observations (Application side)' section confirming pinned v2.1.0, automated prune+selfHeal, and full retry backoff, stating the Application 'is not the problem'; only LOW polish items raised.

expectations.text: Reports overall status as FAIL due to Critical security finding

expectations.text: Does NOT flag the Application itself — it has proper syncPolicy

expectations.text: Does NOT produce false positives on other aspects of this Application

expectations.text: Recommends pinning to a specific tag, commit SHA, or release branch

expectations.text: Severity is Warning (not Critical — it's a best practice violation, not a security vulnerability)

expectations.text: Recommends adding a failureCondition (e.g., result[0] < threshold) and failureLimit

evals.name: Subtle RBAC: looks restricted but has privilege escalation

expectations.text: Flags clusterResourceWhitelist allowing ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding as a privilege escalation risk — the data team can create ClusterRoleBindings that grant themselves (or their apps) cluster-admin
expectations.evidence: F1 CRITICAL quotes L18-21 and walks the full attack: commit a ClusterRoleBinding of cluster-admin to the data-eng default ServiceAccount, which the application-controller applies.

expectations.text: Flags the exec permission in the project role (exec, create) as a security risk — allows terminal access into running pods, which can be used to access node-level resources, service account tokens, and secrets
expectations.evidence: F2 CRITICAL on project.yaml:26 — shell into any pod, bypasses Kubernetes RBAC and audit attribution, exposes env vars, mounted Secret volumes, and the ServiceAccount token.

expectations.text: Does NOT flag sourceRepos or destinations — those are properly restricted
expectations.evidence: Affirms both are genuinely restricted in the intro and the 'Why this passes a casual review' checklist, but then raises F6 MEDIUM against project.yaml:10-14 destinations ('no environment separation ... should be separate projects').

expectations.text: Does NOT flag the Application — it has proper syncPolicy, pinned targetRevision, and retry
expectations.evidence: No finding contradicts the sync policy, pinning, or retry (F10 explicitly acknowledges 'has automated and retry'); Application-side items are LOW hygiene only (finalizer, syncOptions, revisionHistoryLimit, notifications).

expectations.text: Explains why ClusterRole+ClusterRoleBinding in clusterResourceWhitelist is dangerous even when destinations are scoped — the created ClusterRoleBinding applies cluster-wide, not just to the allowed namespaces
expectations.evidence: 'Critically, the destination scoping does not help. destinations restricts spec.destination ... ClusterRoleBinding is cluster-scoped: it has no namespace, so the data-eng/data-staging restriction simply does not apply to it.'

expectations.text: Reports overall status as FAIL or WARN due to the privilege escalation path
expectations.evidence: 'Verdict: two CRITICAL findings (F1 cluster-admin via whitelisted ClusterRoleBinding; F2 exec granted to a group) and one HIGH.'
